jobs.title: Director, Counterparty Credit Risk Models, Global Risk Analytics
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As part of the Group Risk Management team, the Director, Counterparty Credit Risk Analytics leads a team which is responsible for the conceptual design, development, and ongoing maintenance of the mathematical models used for the measurement and capitalization of the counterparty credit risk of RBC's derivative and SFT portfolio. This includes ensuring that the model's underlying methodologies are appropriate and that they are implemented with integrity, to facilitate the effective management of the bank's CCR.

What will you do?

Work with model users to understand their business requirements.
Conduct research, review regulatory requirements and consult with industry stakeholders to evaluate best practices for modeling.
Make recommendations on model methodologies, and develop technical implementation, either for production usage or to serve as a prototype for benchmark testing.
Provide business requirements with technical implementation details and user acceptance criteria to technology teams for production deployment, and validate implementation using independently developed benchmark models.
Document model methodologies, implementation details and testing results, and work with internal validation to facilitate their approval of the models.
Develop tools to assess and monitor model performance, including assumptions and limitations, on an ongoing basis for reporting to the various model monitoring governance committees.
Investigate and remediate modeling issues identified through regular re-reviews, ongoing monitoring or by internal validation.
Recalibrate models on a regular basis.
Re-assessment and testing of models, including assumptions and limitations and benchmarking against alternative models, and documentation of the results in models whitepapers and annual assessments for review by internal validation.

What do you need to succeed?

Must Have:

Broad knowledge of traded products across various asset classes.
Understanding of regulatory requirements and industry best practices for the measurement and management of counterparty credit risk.
Strong analytical and problem solving skills.
Excellent programming skills (e.g., Python).
Strong data management and analysis skills (e.g. SQL and Excel).
Ability to work collaboratively to achieve team goals.
Agility to adapt to changing circumstances in a dynamic environment.
Experience managing a team.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal, especially in the explanation of complex modeling concepts to senior management and regulators.

Nice-to-Have:

Masters in Financial Engineering, or a degree in another quantitative subject such as physics, statistics, mathematics or mathematical finance and/or a relevant professional qualification, with concentration in quantitative methods and/or finance.

What is in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking, to keep growing, and working together to build and deliver trusted reporting to help our stakeholders succeed and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities

Job Skills

Analytical Thinking, Complex Modeling, Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR), Counterparty Risk, Counterparty Risk Management, Financial Engineering, Mathematical Finance, Mathematics Modeling, Model Development, Model Risk, Risk Analytics, Risk Management, Risk Models

Head of Insights Consulting

Halifax, Nova Scotia

Hybrid (2 days a week in office)

Responsibilities also include to lead and design a broad range of complex, mixed-method, and high-impact insights initiatives aimed at answering business questions and identifying opportunities and risks for clients.

Working closely with internal stakeholders, the Head of Insights partners with the Senior Director to support strategic planning, prioritization, and continuous improvement initiatives across the function.

Manage the team capacity, governance, and deployment in a fast-paced environment
Work with internal stakeholders and support the Sr Director with projects triage and prioritization.
Coach and Develop insights talent while maintaining high quality standards through embedded peer review practice
Lead and manage complex and high stakes mixed-method insights projects end-to-end
Be a go-to subject matter expert in:
The development and implementation of high quality proprietary primary research projects
The search and validation of secondary information relevant to the business problem to solve or opportunity to explore, while remaining in the scope of the role’s responsibilities
Tools and techniques facilitating information search and processing including but not limited to AI enabled solutions
Deliver high quality outputs using the combination of information gathered, summarize complex insights findings into short and clear actionable information, adapted to audiences
Work with the team to ensure and increase visibility of insights, supporting customer centric and fact based decision-making and planning. Support clients in owning the insights and taking actions about them
Continuously seek improvement for the team’s activities and operations, keeping up with any emerging tools, techniques and sources, including but not limited to AI
Proactively initiate and recommend insights activities, aiming to “answer questions before they are asked”.
Play an active role in the insights team yearly planning and development of combined activities.
Liaise with senior management to identify information needs and opportunities to optimize the business and deliver insights and key analytics solutions.
This role is a mix of hands on and managerial responsibilities. Will require to partner with external vendors and to collaborate with internal subject matter experts in other fields

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in related fields and min 5 years’ experience in similar role or equivalent combination of education and experience. MSc or MBA an asset
Enthusiasm for online businesses and highly motivated in developing knowledge about various topics and industries. Suitable business acumen expected
Strong experience in scoping / designing mixed-method programs (qual + quant integration)
Ability to set priorities, multi-task, handle pressure and obtain results. Commitment to meeting timelines.
Ability to structure concise and clear results presentations based on large amounts of information
Strong attention to detail and critical thinking.
Must be comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative information and how to combine them.
Knowledge of marketing research, basic statistical analysis and analytics required
Knowledge of various secondary information sources, and capability to continuously seek and learn new sources
More specifically, awareness of web related information and measures and knowledge of AI tools and techniques in the context of insights.
Comfortable in a decentralized structure where results are based on cooperation, collaboration, and influence of others.

The AVP, Strategic Technology Delivery – Claims is responsible for defining and delivering the strategic technology roadmap for Claims and Customer Interaction (CI), serving as the key link between business strategy and technology execution. Partnering closely with business leaders, Technology Services, enterprise architecture, and external vendors, this role oversees the development of technology solutions, business cases, and delivery strategies that support digital transformation and operational excellence.

The AVP leads the end-to-end delivery of complex technology and business transformation initiatives, ensuring investments are executed effectively and deliver measurable business value. jobs.title: Associate director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Associate Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, you will head the Financial Planning & Analysis team at Novo Canada. You will own the budgeting of ex-factory sales and costs, manage operating profit and guide how resources are allocated, giving the President, CFO and Executive Team the clarity to decide and act. Your work helps the affiliate reach its financial and strategic goals and keeps our products available to the people who rely on them.

What You’ll Bring

You combine strong financial expertise with the leadership to build a high-performing team.

You Will Also Bring

A bachelor/master’s degree in business administration, finance, business economics, accounting or auditing.
At least 5 years of experience in finance, with proven success in numbers-driven analysis, planning and reporting.
Experience presenting to senior management and executives, and the ability to explain quantitative analysis clearly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and a track record of planning, prioritising and following through while proactively managing risks.
A proven track record in complex, cross-affiliate project management.
An understanding of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and internal controls.
Proficiency in SAP, Business Warehouse and Excel.
In-depth understanding of the global budgeting process at Novo or a company of similar size.
A leadership style that builds trust, gives honest feedback, sets clear priorities and keeps things simple, especially through change.

What You’ll Do

You will lead the full financial planning cycle for Novo Canada and the commercial terms that connect our products to customers.

Your Work Will Help To

Lead, develop and plan the work of the Financial Planning & Analysis team, including hiring, succession, individual development plans and performance dialogue, and manage the team budget.
Oversee the affiliate P&L, including ex-factory sales, cost of goods sold and total operating costs, and own the total ex-factory sales forecast and targets.
Run the annual budget and rolling estimate processes, challenging submissions, ensuring compliance with corporate guidelines and anchoring approved targets across the business, while advising the President and CFO on resource allocation and supporting the Executive Team’s cost target.
Deliver monthly and quarterly reporting to management, the region and headquarters on sales, expenses and operating profit, flagging issues early and proposing corrective actions.
Own gross-to-net including rebate accruals under provincial Product Listing Agreements, and weekly sales performance reporting.
Lead priority initiatives for Financial Planning & Analysis and contribute to value-creation projects across Executive Team areas, and work with other affiliates to share best practices and keep planning simple and value-adding.

Who You’ll Work With

You will join Finance & Operations at Novo Canada as a member of the Finance & Operations Leadership Team. You will lead the Financial Planning & Analysis team, which you will help shape and grow.

Your closest partners will be the President, the CFO and the Executive Team. You will bring a financial perspective to the commercial teams, joining their management meetings, and support Line of Business colleagues with managing investments, month-end closing and training on financial processes.

You will also work with regional finance, headquarters, the Pricing Committee and colleagues in other affiliates, and directly with buyers at key wholesalers. These relationships let you turn numbers into clear, timely decisions.

What You Can Expect Here

You will take on a leadership role where your voice shapes decisions at executive level. The role gives you a broad view of the business, from budgets and operating profit to trade strategy, pricing and launches, and the opportunity to build new skills through cross-functional and cross-affiliate work.
You will be trusted to own your area and make decisions, with clear performance expectations and a culture that rewards results. You will also help your team thrive and grow through coaching, development plans and ongoing dialogue about performance and development.

What We Offer

At Novo, you'll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

Position Purpose

The role works on behalf of a program, function, department, division, or Territory independently executing a range of financial responsibilities: developing and implementing accurate, timely, and complete spreadsheets and templates, budget, and accounting documents.

Key Accountabilities

Lead the development, monitoring, and forecasting of annual budgets for large Ministry Units (MUs) and territorial departments, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and budgeting guidelines.
Analyze financial results, budget variances, and reporting packages to identify risks, trends, and key issues, providing actionable insights to senior leadership and department stakeholders.
Support long-term financial planning by developing forecasts, evaluating future funding requirements, and advising on financial sustainability.
Ensure compliance of project budgets, expenditures, and financial reporting with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) regulations and internal policies governing donor and international development funding.
Review project progress, funding commitments, and financial performance to confirm adequate resources are available and organizational obligations are met.
Provide financial expertise, guidance, training, and consultative support to leaders and project teams on budgeting, reporting, compliance, and financial management practices.
Collaborate with internal departments and external stakeholders, including auditors, funders, vendors, and service providers, to gather information, resolve issues, and support financial operations.
Prepare and oversee complex financial transactions, journal entries, payment approvals, and other financial activities to ensure accurate and timely processing.
Contribute to business process improvements and system enhancements by assessing operational requirements, documenting changes, and supporting the implementation of effective financial practices.
Support donor-funded initiatives through financial analysis, funding oversight, trend identification, stakeholder presentations, and participation in special projects and departmental activities.

Education And Experience Qualifications

Completion of a post-secondary degree or diploma (minimum three-year program) in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Minimum five (5) years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, budgeting, financial analysis, or a related field.
Demonstrated expertise in financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial controls.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify risks, evaluate options, and recommend effective solutions.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships and provide consultative support to diverse stakeholders.
Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment while managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.
Exceptional attention to detail, accuracy, and organizational skills, with a strong commitment to customer service and continuous improvement.
High level of integrity, professionalism, and adaptability, including the ability to navigate change, exercise sound judgment, and work effectively with complex financial information and varying reporting standards.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $85,321.60 to $106,641.60 with a maximum of $127,982.40.

jobs.title: Director of Finance & Administration
jobs.description:
Director of Finance & Administration

Groundswell Food Group, Inc. (DBA Mitsoh)
Location: Remote
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
About Mitsoh

Mitsoh is building a new generation of clean-protein foods rooted in tradition and made for modern lifestyles. Our products are crafted with a focus on high-quality ingredients, nutritional integrity, and responsible sourcing. As a rapidly growing CPG food company, we operate with world-class manufacturing and food safety standards aligned with GFSI-recognized programs.

We are seeking a hands-on and strategic Director of Finance & Administration to build the financial infrastructure, controls, and administrative systems required to scale Mitsoh into a world-class food manufacturing company and consumer brand.

Position Overview

The Director of Finance & Administration is responsible for leading Mitsoh’s finance, accounting, and administrative functions, including financial reporting, planning and analysis, product costing, cash management, HR and payroll administration, and business systems.

Reporting to the CEO and leading a small team, this role partners closely with operations, supply chain, and commercial teams to drive margin visibility, cost discipline, and data-driven decision-making across both the manufacturing and brand sides of the business. This is a builder’s role — equally comfortable setting strategy with leadership and rolling up sleeves to close the month.

Key Responsibilities

Accounting & Financial Reporting

Own the full accounting cycle, including month-end close, reconciliations, and preparation of accurate, timely financial statements

Maintain the integrity of the general ledger, chart of accounts, and financial controls as the company scales

Manage accounts receivable, accounts payable, collections, and customer/vendor account reconciliation

Oversee inventory accounting, including raw materials, WIP, finished goods, and reconciliation of physical counts to system records

Manage external accountant, audit, and tax relationships, including year-end preparation and regulatory filings

Financial Planning & Analysis

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, and scenario planning aligned with company growth objectives

Deliver monthly reporting packages with variance analysis and plain-language commentary for leadership and the board

Build KPI dashboards and reporting across revenue, margin, cash, and operational performance

Provide financial modeling and analysis to support pricing, capital investment, and growth decisions

Product Costing & Margin Management

Own standard costing for manufactured products, including BOMs, yields, labor, and overhead absorption

Analyze cost variances between standard and actual production performance and drive corrective visibility

Deliver margin analysis by product, channel, and customer across DTC, retail, and distributor networks

Partner with operations and supply chain on COGS reduction, waste, and yield improvement initiatives

Revenue, Trade & Channel Finance

Manage revenue recognition and channel-specific billing across DTC, retail, and distributor accounts

Track and validate trade spend, promotions, chargebacks, and distributor deductions

Support commercial teams with customer profitability analysis and pricing guidance

Monitor and reconcile e-commerce platform payouts, fees, and settlements

Cash Management & Treasury

Own cash flow forecasting and working capital management, including inventory, receivables, and payables cycles

Manage banking relationships, credit facilities, and financing arrangements

Support capital raising, government funding programs, and grant applications as required

Ensure disciplined spend management and approval controls across the organization

HR & Payroll Administration

Administer payroll, group benefits, and related remittances and filings

Oversee employee onboarding, offboarding, records, and HR policy administration

Ensure compliance with employment standards and related regulatory requirements

Support leadership on compensation planning and people-related processes as the team grows

Business Systems & IT Administration

Own the company’s ERP and financial systems, ensuring data integrity and effective integration across order management, inventory, and accounting

Manage software subscriptions, IT vendors, and technology spend

Drive automation and process improvement across finance and administrative workflows

Support the selection and implementation of new systems as the company scales

Leadership & Team Development

Build, lead, and develop the finance and administration team

Establish clear processes, documentation, and cross-training across the function

Serve as a trusted business partner to the CEO and leadership team

Foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement

Qualifications

CPA designation required

8–10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership roles within a CPG food or beverage manufacturing environment

Strong experience with product costing, inventory accounting, and manufacturing finance

Experience across DTC, retail, and distributor channels, including trade spend and deduction management

Proven track record leading budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting for a growing company

Experience administering payroll, benefits, and HR processes in a small-to-mid-size company

Strong ERP and systems experience, including implementations or integrations

Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills

Core Competencies

Financial leadership and business partnership

Manufacturing costing and margin management

Planning, forecasting, and analysis

Cash and working capital management

Controls, compliance, and accuracy

Systems and process improvement

Team building and development

Clear communication with financial and non-financial audiences

Additional Information

This is a remote role. Periodic travel to Mitsoh’s Leduc, Alberta facility and operational partners may be required for planning cycles, inventory counts, and leadership meetings.

What We’re Looking For

Mitsoh is looking for a builder. The ideal candidate is technically strong, highly operational, and energized by creating financial and administrative infrastructure from the ground up. This leader will bring the discipline, visibility, and systems required to scale a modern food company — while staying hands-on in a lean, fast-moving environment.
